clue.text: Eminent lady writing tot a letter

parts.note: to tot up is to count, add up a column of figures
ess is the spelt-out name of the letter S

explanation.surface: A grand noblewoman is pictured penning a note to a small child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a toddler receiving the letter, but it is the verb, as in totting up a bill; 'writing' merely links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A countess is a noblewoman, the wife of an earl or count, so a titled eminent lady.

clue.text: The wild pear harvest

indicators.note: wild suggests something unruly and untamed, so the letters of the next word are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone gathers in the crop from an uncultivated pear tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To reap is to cut and gather a crop, a verb synonym for harvest.

clue.text: Dressing right as the cup holder

parts.note: a dressing for food, such as a salad dressing, is a sauce

explanation.surface: A salad dressing is apparently the correct holder for a cup, as in a trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link word joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A saucer is the small dish that a teacup stands on, so it literally holds the cup.

clue.text: Source of sandalwood?

parts.note: read not as the fragrant timber but as a tree from which sandals would come, punning on a wooden form put inside footwear

explanation.surface: A question about where fragrant sandalwood comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoetree is a shaped block, often wooden, kept inside footwear; whimsically it is a tree growing shoes such as sandals.

clue.text: Public schoolboy getting shut in a car by mistake

indicators.note: a mistake implies things put the wrong way round, so the letters of the preceding words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A private-school pupil is accidentally locked inside a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: A Carthusian is a pupil at Charterhouse, a famous English fee-paying school (in Britain called a public school); 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils of Charterhouse School are called Carthusians, so one is a public schoolboy.

clue.text: The chaperone expected a girl to rise

parts.note: something expected is due, as a train due at noon

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading upwards, so the girl's name is turned round

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A chaperone anticipates that a young woman will get up.
explanation.walkthrough: ANNA reads the same either way, so the reversal changes nothing on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: A duenna is an older woman who acts as chaperone to young women, especially in Spain.

clue.text: A lot rent accommodation, all for freedom

indicators.note: accommodation suggests letters adjusted and rearranged to fit, so the preceding words are reworked

explanation.surface: Many people pay rent for housing, supposedly all in the name of liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodation' looks like the housing being rented, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tolerant favours letting others act freely, a descriptive paraphrase of being permissive.

clue.text: Ditch such a coat

definitions.meaning: a long narrow excavated channel in the ground
a belted waterproof coat in military style, named from First World War soldiers

explanation.surface: Someone is told to throw away a particular style of coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ditch' reads as a verb meaning discard, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A trench is a dug ditch, and a trench coat is the classic belted raincoat.

clue.text: The man with a dog to collect

parts.note: he is the pronoun standing for a man
a pup is a young dog

explanation.surface: A man with his dog comes to pick something up.
explanation.definitionFit: To heap up is to pile together or amass, a phrasal synonym for collect.

clue.text: Speak irritably, or quietly answer back

indicators.note: back tells us to read the preceding pieces from end to start

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Advice to either bark at someone or reply softly with a retort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the run PANS round; 'answer back' reads as cheek, but 'back' is the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: To snap is to speak sharply and irritably, as in snapping at someone.

clue.text: Fruit for an old miner's daughter

definitions.meaning: a small seedless citrus fruit like a tangerine
the darling of the American folk song, daughter of a forty-niner gold prospector

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit set aside for the daughter of a former coal miner.
explanation.walkthrough: The song 'Oh My Darling, Clementine' tells of a miner's daughter; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Clementine names both the citrus fruit and the miner's daughter in the well-known ballad.

clue.text: From September, berries form the main food of a North African

indicators.note: from says the answer is drawn out of the words that follow, straddling them

explanation.surface: From autumn onwards berries are the staple diet of someone in North Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the end of 'September' and the start of 'berries'; 'form the main food of' is surface padding linking to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Berbers are an indigenous people of North Africa, so one is a North African.

clue.text: A drab block specially built for teachers' use

indicators.note: something specially built is made up afresh, so the letters of the preceding words are reassembled

explanation.surface: A dull slab has been made to order for schoolteachers.
explanation.definitionFit: A blackboard is the dark writing surface teachers chalk on in class, an item made for their use.

clue.text: Drinking song sung at Christmas all round America

indicators.note: all round says the first piece encloses the next one

parts.note: a carol is a song sung at Christmas
USA is the abbreviation for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A festive drinking song sung across America at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: A carousal is a bout of drunken revelry, so the noun drinking in the sense of a drinking session.

clue.text: Radiant bishop in support

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a stay is a prop or support, as in a corset stay
RR, Right Reverend, is the title abbreviation of a bishop

explanation.surface: A glowing clergyman provides backing to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: A bishop is styled the Right Reverend, abbreviated RR.
explanation.definitionFit: Starry means shining like stars, a close synonym of radiant.

clue.text: Some soldiers wheeled around and came back

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British army corps, so some soldiers
to wheel around is to turn

explanation.surface: A troop of soldiers turned about and marched home.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Returned means came back, a direct past-tense synonym.

clue.text: A gorge subject to pollution

definitions.meaning: a narrow pass or ravine between hills
to make impure or dirty, as a verb

explanation.surface: A ravine is threatened by contamination.
explanation.definitionFit: A defile is a narrow mountain pass, and to defile is to pollute or desecrate.

clue.text: This is sure to have an inflationary effect!

definitions.text: This is sure to have an inflationary effect!

parts.words: This is sure to have an inflationary effect!
parts.note: reads like economics, but means a photographic device that blows up images to a bigger size

explanation.surface: A warning about some policy that will surely push up prices.
explanation.definitionFit: An enlarger is the darkroom apparatus that projects a negative to make bigger prints, so it inflates pictures.

clue.text: Forces relax in quarters

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: W and S, west and south, are two quarters of the compass
to rest is to relax

explanation.surface: Armed forces take it easy in their barracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' looks like living accommodation for troops, but it gives two compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrests means forces or wrenches away by twisting, a verb synonym for forces.

clue.text: Dealer taking a certain measure about a chest

indicators.note: about says the first piece goes round the next

parts.note: a meter is a measuring instrument, such as a gas meter
an ark is a chest or coffer, as in the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: A trader takes measurements around a box.
explanation.definitionFit: A marketer sells goods in a market, so a trader or dealer.

clue.text: Putting a note in the pool would be fine

indicators.note: in places the note inside the pool

parts.note: a mere is a lake or pool
C is one of the musical notes

explanation.surface: Dropping a musical note into the swimming pool would be acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' reads as 'all right' but is the verb meaning to penalise; 'Putting' and 'would be' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To amerce is an old legal verb meaning to punish with a fine.

clue.text: Sort of old pottery the French mix together

parts.note: Ming is the porcelain of the Chinese Ming dynasty
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Antique pottery that French people combine.
explanation.definitionFit: To mingle is to blend or mix together.

clue.text: Many a Northerner exhibits charm

parts.note: M, the Roman numeral for a thousand, stands for many
a Scot comes from Scotland, the north of Britain

explanation.surface: Plenty of northern folk display allure.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a lucky charm, an object or creature thought to bring good fortune.

clue.text: The gardener's joy makes for an easy life

definitions.meaning: a planted area of roses, literally a gardener's delight
the idiom for a comfortable, carefree existence

explanation.surface: A rose bed delights the gardener and makes life pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes for' is a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a flower bed of roses; idiomatically, life is no bed of roses when it is hard.

clue.text: Against a transport system change

parts.note: v, versus, means against
RY is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Opposition to a transport network alteration.
explanation.definitionFit: To vary is to change or alter, a verb synonym.

clue.text: A hollow farewell!

definitions.meaning: a valley, a low-lying hollow between hills

explanation.surface: A goodbye that rings empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hollow' reads as an adjective meaning insincere, but it is the noun for a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A vale is a valley, and vale is Latin for farewell.

clue.text: Panic, being about a hundred short

indicators.note: about says the first piece goes round the next

parts.note: a scare is a sudden panic
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Alarm spreads because supplies are about a hundred down.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarce means in short supply, so short in the sense of lacking.

clue.text: Ought with little hesitation to assume responsibility

parts.note: ought and should both express obligation
er is the small sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone should take on duties without much pause.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoulder a burden is to take it on, an idiom for accepting responsibility.
